system.name: Gated Attention
system.one_liner: Empirical study of gates inside softmax attention for LLMs: a head-specific sigmoid gate after SDPA improves quality, stabilises training and removes attention sinks.

content.variant_note: a gate-position schematic on the left and two result plots (bar charts, loss curves) sharing its colours; no process runs through the three parts
content.argues: Of five places where a gate can sit in an attention layer, the one after the SDPA output gives the largest perplexity and MMLU gains and a smoother, spike-free training loss.
content.subject: An attention layer drawn bottom-up with five colour-coded gate positions, beside bar charts of PPL and MMLU change per position and training-loss curves of baseline versus gated model.

lessons.what_to_learn: When a study varies where one operation is inserted, mark each candidate position with a coloured, labelled circle on the architecture and reuse those colours in the result plots, so the schematic works as the legend of the results.
lessons.suits: Ablation or design-space studies of insertion points (gates, norms, adapters, skip links) whose results are a few bars and one training curve.

evidence: Gating after SDPA (G1) yields the best overall results.
Gating results in lower final loss and substantially enhanced training stability, mitigating loss spikes.
we introduce gating at distinct positions (Fig. 1): after the query (G4), key (G3), and value projections (G2)

summary: This paper studies gating inside softmax attention for LLMs and finds that a head-specific sigmoid gate after scaled dot-product attention improves perplexity and MMLU, stabilises training and mitigates attention sinks. Figure 1 is a three-part teaser. Left: an attention layer drawn bottom-up (Query, Key and Value layers, SDPA, Concat, dense layer) with five coloured circles G1 to G5 marking where a gate can be inserted, G1 flagged Most Effective!. Middle: two bar charts of average PPL and MMLU show each position's change from a dashed baseline in the matching colours. Right: training-loss curves in which the grey baseline spikes while the blue G1-gated run stays lower and smooth.
summary_zh: 论文研究 LLM 注意力中的门控，发现 SDPA 之后的逐头 sigmoid 门最有效。图1分三块：左为自下而上的注意力层与 G1–G5 门控位置，中为各位置 PPL 与 MMLU 变化柱图，右为训练损失曲线，颜色对应。
notes: The pre-screen kept only model-anatomy with 'tables-numbers' data; two thirds of the figure are measured plots, so the record puts contribution-mosaic first and keeps model-anatomy for the left schematic. The grey and blue shades of the plots are plotting-library colours given at 0.5 opacity in the SVG.
